name: Ear: Dark Skin Tone
baseMeaning: Human ear emoji. The dark skin tone modifier is applied to the ear.
tldr: 👂🏿 Ear with a dark skin tone. Always a deliberate pick, and one that needs context to land.

contextMeanings.meaning: Shows the same artwork as the untoned version, with the dark skin tone applied to the ear.
The gesture reads the same as the untoned version; the dark skin tone makes it a deliberate statement with real weight behind it.
In a dating thread the gesture is unchanged; the tone makes it a strong statement, and a wrong one lands badly.
In a work thread the gesture is unchanged, and the dark skin tone reads as deliberate enough that the choice itself is noticed.

platformNotes.note: On iOS 👂🏿 renders as one combined glyph with the tone applied. The dark swatch is the last one in Apple's picker, and it is also the one where the rendering difference between clients is largest: the same emoji can look like a noticeably different person depending on which font drew it.

WhatsApp applies the dark modifier on current builds and lists it last, so it takes a deliberate scroll. Older Android builds of WhatsApp fall back to the untoned glyph, and because the dark swatch is the most conspicuous of the five when it does render, the difference between the two is the one people notice.

Twemoji renders 👂🏿 with the dark swatch intact, and it is the tone most often used deliberately on the platform, so it is also the one most likely to be screenshotted out of context and read as a comment on whoever is in the picture.

Slack's own emoji font renders the dark swatch with less contrast against the darker themes than the phone version does. On a dark background the tone can lose definition entirely, which is worth knowing before you conclude that somebody sent something else.

Discord uses Twemoji and applies the modifier cleanly. As with the other dark-swatch uses, the interesting failure mode is not rendering but reuse: 👂🏿 forwarded into a channel it was not meant for keeps its meaning as a statement and loses its context.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z uses 👂🏿 as a clear statement of self, and is also the cohort most alert to its use about other people. Because the swatch is unmistakable, the reaction to a misused 👂🏿 in this cohort is fast and rarely subtle.

Millennials use 👂🏿 when they are representing themselves, and read the tone as personal. It is also the tone most often borrowed to depict somebody else, which is where it turns from a self-description into a comment on somebody's appearance.

Gen X rarely changes the tone, so 👂🏿 mostly shows up as self-representation. Older clients in this cohort also flatten it more often, so the glyph a sender saw is not always the glyph a recipient saw.

warnings.title: Do not use the dark swatch as a joke about skin
warnings.description: 👂🏿 is the tone most often used to make a point about somebody's appearance. Used about someone other than the sender, it is read as a comment on their skin rather than as the gesture.

seoTitle: 👂🏿 Ear Dark Skin Tone Emoji Meaning - What Does 👂🏿 Mean?
seoDescription: What does the ear emoji 👂🏿 mean? Ear showing a single human ear in side profile, the inner folds curved inward. Covers the dark skin tone variant, the misread it invites, and how to reply.

longForm.overview:
Reaching 👂🏿 takes work, because it is the last swatch in the tone list, so reaching it means scrolling or swiping past four others. That is worth knowing, because it changes what the emoji means in a thread. 👂🏿 is Ear with a dark skin tone, a single human ear in side profile, the inner folds curved inward, and it is doing the same job as 👂: listening, hearing something, or paying attention.

But a tone that someone went looking for is not a tone that gets skimmed. The most deliberately chosen of the five, because getting there is the most work. In a group chat, 👂🏿 tends to get a second look, and it tends to get one for a reason — either because it genuinely represents the sender, or because the sender wanted it to. The difference between those two is not visible from the emoji alone, which is the single most important thing to understand about this variant.

The situations it turns up in are the family ones, unchanged by the tone, and the trap is the same one the rest of the set has: it gets taken as "sounds good" when it usually means "I am listening to you right now", because the ear alone signals attention rather than agreement. The neighbouring glyph people reach for instead is 🦻 Ear with Hearing Aid — the hearing aid version adds the device behind the ear and gets used when hearing itself is the subject.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
The gesture is the same one 👂 makes, so the family habits carry straight over. What changes with 👂🏿 is who tends to send it and what they are assuming about the reader.

Because it is the last swatch, 👂🏿 shows up where the tone was the point: an avatar, a profile picture, an introduction of oneself, a reaction that is meant to carry the sender's own appearance. It appears in telling a friend you are on a call listening, and in reacting when someone says something surprising.

It is also, for the same reason, the tone most likely to be deployed as a joke about someone's skin, which is the context where it stops being harmless. 👂🏿 used about someone other than the sender, with no context, is the version of this emoji that causes real offence — and the reason is not the gesture but the fact that the tone was chosen to make a point.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
The family rule applies first, and it is the one spelled out above: the standard misread of this glyph belongs to 👂 itself, and every tone in this family inherits it.

The trap for 👂🏿 is the obvious one, and it is worth stating plainly: the darkest swatch is the one most often used as a joke about skin. Because it takes a deliberate scroll to reach, the emoji reads as a statement about somebody, and if the sender is not the somebody, it lands as a comment on their appearance. Do not use 👂🏿 to depict another person without a reason you would be comfortable explaining out loud.

Beyond that, skip it when the moment is light enough that a swatch with this much weight will outweigh the sentence. 👂🏿 gets a second look in every thread it lands in, and not every message can afford that.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply with 🏿 if the sender was representing themselves — matching the darkest swatch is one of the more concrete ways to say you saw what they chose. 👂 is fine when the tone was incidental.

If the tone was pointed — if 👂🏿 was deployed as a joke about somebody's skin — the reply is a sentence, not an emoji. Nothing mirrors that well, and a mirrored emoji makes the joke land twice.

faqs.question: What does 👂🏿 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 👂🏿 is Ear with a dark skin tone. The gesture reads as listening, hearing something, or paying attention, and the swatch is the heaviest of the five.

faqs.question: Is 👂🏿 a deliberate choice?
faqs.answer: Almost always. It is the last swatch in the tone list, so reaching it means scrolling or swiping past four others. That is why 👂🏿 gets a second look in a thread while 👂 does not.

faqs.question: What does 👂🏿 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: The gesture reads the same as it does from anyone else. The skin tone is not a gendered signal on 👂.

faqs.question: Is 👂🏿 offensive?
faqs.answer: It can be, and it is the tone most often used as a joke about skin. It is the tone most often used to make a point about someone’s skin, which is why it never travels without context. Used to depict the sender, it is one of the most personal choices in the emoji set.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 👂🏿 and 👂?
faqs.answer: The swatch, and it matters more here than for the other tones. 👂 is the tone-less version, and it is the right pick whenever the sender is not the person being shown.
